notes.text: Festo Didactic FactoryViews and MES4 deployed along with xampp bundle an Apache web server with PHP. The bundled version of PHP is vulnerable to the two critical vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (commonly referred to as PHP2Shell). These vulnerabilities allow an attacker to remotely execute code on the FactoryViews or xampp host system.
notes.title: Summary

notes.text: A successful attack on a vulnerable PHP installation allows the attacker to remotely execute malicious code on the FactoryViews or xampp host system with the privileges of the user account running the server application.
notes.title: Impact

notes.text:
The xampp versions installed with older deployments of MES4 run PHP versions up to 7.3. These versions are out-of-support and no patches have been made available.
Users can apply the mitigation measures recommended by the PHP foundation:
- CVE-2026-109618: Set memory_limit=-1 in php.ini.
- CVE-2026-109619: Set "session.upload_progress.enabled=0" in php.ini. Additionally, the setting "MaxConnectionsPerChild 1" can be added to the end of httpd-xampp.conf. Note that this will have a significant negative impact on performance.
Users might also consider adding firewall rules to the Windows host system which restrict communication with httpd.exe from sources other than the HMI panels of manual workstations.
notes.title: Mitigation

notes.text:
Festo recommends updating FactoryViews to version 1.12.2 through the "Versions" page of the FactoryViews control panel. Versions of FactoryViews prior to 1.12 must first be updated to 1.12 available for download here: https://www.festo.com/de/de/support-portal-specific?query=factoryviews&groupId=4&productName=factoryviews&documentId=659952

For MES4 with xampp no fix is available. Please apply the mitigation measures.
notes.title: Remediation

notes.text:
As part of a security strategy, Festo recommends the following general defense measures to reduce the risk of exploits: 
- Use controllers and devices only in a protected environment to minimize network exposure and ensure that they are not accessible from outside.
- Use firewalls to protect and separate the control system network from other networks.
- Use VPN (Virtual Private Networks) tunnels if remote access is required.
- Activate and apply user management and password features.
- Use encrypted communication links.
- Limit the access to both development and control system by physical means, operating system features, etc. 
- Protect both development and control systems by using up-to-date virus detection solutions.

Festo strongly recommends minimizing and protecting network access to connected devices with state-of-the-art techniques and processes. 
To ensure secure operation follow the recommendations in the product manuals.
notes.title: General recommendations

notes.text: PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).
notes.title: CVE description

notes.text: The vulnerability originates from error handling during out-of-memory conditions. When request processing is aborted, request-owned memory structures may remain in an inconsistent state. Subsequent cleanup operations can access corrupted internal state, resulting in memory corruption that can be leveraged for code execution.
notes.title: Technical Details

notes.text: Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated remote code execution with the privileges of the user account running the PHP process. This can result in compromise of confidentiality, integrity and availability of the affected system.
notes.title: Impact

remediations.details:
Install patch 1.12.2 through the "Versions" page of the FactoryViews control panel on version 1.12.0 or 1.12.1.

Versions of FactoryViews prior to 1.12 must first be updated to 1.12 available for download here: https://www.festo.com/de/de/support-portal-specific?query=factoryviews&groupId=4&productName=factoryviews&documentId=659952

The xampp versions installed with older deployments of MES4 run PHP versions up to 7.3. These version are out-of-support and no patches have been made available.
Users can apply the mitigation measures recommended by the PHP foundation:
Set memory_limit=-1 in php.ini.
Users might also consider adding firewall rules to the Windows host system which restrict communication with httpd.exe from sources other than the HMI panels of manual workstations.

notes.text: PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).
notes.title: CVE description

notes.text: The vulnerability arises from stale request-owned global state that outlives the request memory to which it points. When a subsequent request handled by the same worker process reuses that state, PHP can access invalid memory, resulting in memory corruption and a potential path to code execution.
notes.title: Technical Details

notes.text: Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated remote code execution with the privileges of the user account running the PHP process. This can result in compromise of confidentiality, integrity and availability of the affected system.
